answer: In the PCA of the forms of capital over hundred-year time slices, PC1 during the Younger Bronze Age (1100-500 BCE) is at its peak value exactly at the beginning of the period — PC1 at 1100 BCE is strongly positive (≈ +4.45) and markedly HIGHER than at every subsequent horizon (1000 BCE ≈ +2.17, 900 ≈ +1.65, 800 ≈ +1.91, 700 ≈ +1.25, 600 ≈ +0.83, 500 ≈ +0.82; mean of 1000-500 BCE ≈ +1.44), i.e., PC1 at 1100 BCE exceeds the later-slice mean by ≈ +3.01 (per-slice differences +2.28 to +3.64) and then declines steadily across the period. Interpreted on the loadings-defined axis (single shared PCA on the 12 z-scored forms-of-capital slices; PC1 explains 31.8% of variance and loads positively on social Copper&Gold +0.40, cultural Pottery decoration +0.38, economic Depot hoards +0.34, symbolic Hatchets&Swords +0.30 and Daggers +0.28, economic Monument Size +0.24, symbolic House Size +0.23, social Monument Count +0.19, negatively on Pottery form −0.36, Axes&Celts −0.26 and Amber −0.26), 1100 BCE represents a pronounced peak of accumulated social/symbolic/economic capital (rich in copper and gold, depot hoards, daggers, large houses, large/abundant monuments, decorated pottery), after which this capital-complexity signal drops substantially and stays low through 1000-500 BCE. The YBA-only refit gives the same substantive reading (1100 BCE is the extreme outlier on the capital-accumulation axis; the sign is reversed only by the arbitrary PCA eigenvector orientation).

payload.hypothesis: During the Younger Bronze Age (1100-500 BCE), the hundred-year-slice PCA on the forms of capital has PC1 strongly positive and at its highest at 1100 BCE (PC1 ~ +4.45) and markedly higher than at all later horizons (1000 BCE ~ +2.17, 900 ~ +1.65, 800 ~ +1.91, 700 ~ +1.25, 600 ~ +0.83, 500 ~ +0.82; mean ~ +1.44), i.e., PC1 at 1100 BCE is ~ +3.0 higher than the average of the 1000-500 BCE slices and declines across the period. On the loadings-defined axis (positive Copper&Gold, Pottery decoration, Depot, Hatchets&Swords, Daggers, Monument Size, House Size, Monument Count), 1100 BCE is a peak of accumulated social/symbolic/economic capital that then drops substantially and stays low through 1000-500 BCE.
payload.workflow: 1) Loaded capital.csv and parsed German comma-decimal Z-values; verified 39 hundred-year slices (BCE 4300->500, step 100), 0 NAs, YBA window = 7 slices (1100,1000,900,800,700,600,500 BCE). Cross-checked identical raw values vs time_series_data.csv at the 100-yr marks (444/444). 2) Single shared PCA on the 12 Z columns (all 39 slices), centered (verified corr 1.0000 vs uncentered => z-scores already standardized); computed PC1 scores, loadings, evr via numpy SVD. 3) Compared PC1 at 1100 BCE (baseline anchor, first YBA slice) vs each later slice 1000-500 BCE and vs their mean; reported signed differences with loadings to fix axis orientation. 4) Documented sensitivity: PCA refit on the 7-slice YBA subset (same substantive axis, flipped sign). 5) Wrote results to analysis/results_YBA_PC1.json. No paper figure numerics assumed; only computed values used.
